LOCAL RESEARCH PROTOTYPE · POPPY 1.2.0

Virtual photon-counting bench

A physical-optics rehearsal for a phase-mask emulator of the two 63-site structures. Explore how fibre alignment and a quadratic wavefront error affect the same fixed classifier.

Simulation, not physical validation. The optical calibration is assumed, all measurements are synthetic, and these scenarios have no new rigorous error certificate. This uses the changed-frequency second-order design, not the original fourth-order-only experiment.

633 nm laser→63 finite phase cells→100 mm Fourier lens→Gaussian fibre mode→Photon counter

Gaussian illumination and diffraction are modeled. One of 64 square cells is blocked. An ideal relay places the phase mask in the lens pupil. An ideal added amplitude mask is computed once for the centered model and held fixed; its implementation by real hardware is unvalidated. The known structures are encoded as phases; this is not an unknown-material reconstruction.

Negative control: both labels use the same A mask. Around 50% balanced error is expected because these distributions are identical; this is not successful A/B separation.

Intervals are per scenario and hypothesis; they are not simultaneous guarantees. Scenarios share phase draws. Zero observed errors does not prove zero true error. These intervals quantify sampling uncertainty inside this simulator, not hardware performance. The plots show static masks; the trial simulations include independent phase fluctuations. The quadratic phase coefficient is not RMS wavefront error: phase = 2π × coefficient × r² / (λ × (0.8 mm)²).

Checks on the calculation

The detector simulation uses Poisson arrivals, 0.125 dark counts per 5 ms gate, and 22 ns nonparalyzable dead time. Renewal sampling is checked against the analytic gamma waiting-time law. The source is independent of the displayed trial outcomes; the score, threshold and calibration are not fitted to those outcomes.

Assumptions that still need laboratory measurements
  • Actual phase levels, phase/amplitude coupling, pixel gaps and crosstalk.
  • Measured illumination, amplitude compensation, polarization and relay/lens response.
  • Detector efficiency, afterpulsing, inter-gate memory and timestamps.
  • Full phase law and independence of settled snapshots.

Only an actual measurement can establish agreement with the apparatus. POPPY is a scalar diffraction model. REA audited the software package; it did not validate the physics.
